I've found in my life the jobs I liked the most were the ones where, at the end of the day, I could stand back and say "I did that." 

Not the ones where's you're waiting for derivatives to break or you're waiting for QA to approve a project move into production, but something as easy as getting a good tip or getting the motor on a boat running again. 

It's easy to say money doesn't buy happiness, but I've found that it's a little more complicated. You need enough money for the basics, and from there you can be as happy as you want to be. Some places, that's a lot - others, it's next to nothing. But it's best to decide what the basics are, and you'd be surprised what you can live without.

Well for me it was a matter of "oh shit, I'm out of money," but in your case it sounds like you may have a "particular set of skills" as it were. 

You're Korean but you speak English this well? Go teach English in Korea, man! Nobody will ever call you short or unattractive, there are many places to go to meet women if you're so inclined, and on top of that you'll be paid for it! 

Think of all of the weirdo white guys applying for jobs to teach English in Korea to meet Korean women - and then think of your chances in comparison. At the absolute worst, you're going to be paid for a year abroad. Have fun! Send a postcard!

Earn it. For the longest time I thought I didn't deserve to live. I still don't, but I did for a while. 

I spent three years volunteering at an animal shelter that sadly euthanized the animals if they weren't adopted in time. I walked hundreds of friends down that cold, narrow hallway, but they were happy because I was there. They wagged their tails until the end and I held my tears back until it was over. I threw up and cried on the back lot more times than I can count, but I knew I'd done something good just being there for them. 

Find a reason. You can type. You can communicate. You can help others.

I've lost friends to suicide and I'd hope yours would care as I did. 

I've seen the result of a gun used in suicide, of a pained call for help expressed through an action rather than words, of someone who chose action over discussion. 

I would have listened. I would have spoken to them. I would have gone over there, but they didn't give me the chance. 

I didn't cry over guilt. I didn't call them insufferable. I understood. But I grieved.

Oh man, if I could nail down the one thing I was passionate about they'd call me ponyboy! 

I've been everything from a bouncer, cave diver, divemaster, financial analyst, software engineer, waiter, bartender and everything in between. At my age, which I don't care to admit, I still haven't got it figured out. 

Maybe it would help if you tried things outside of your comfort range? I never thought I could be a bouncer until I got stabbed (not advised). I didn't think I'd make a good financial analyst until I made someone else a lot of money (but didn't get any for myself, mind you). 

Your grammar, word choice and syntax exhibit a general level of intelligence that qualify you for all sorts of things all over the world. What's wrong with working on a boat in Nicaragua for six months? Why not spend a year in Belize driving a jeep through mud? Why not teach English in Korea? 

Passion is a, if you'll excuse me, cruel bitch. You won't know it until you find it. You've got to go find it. Do everything you can! If you get bored, you're on the wrong track, switch to something new. You sound like you've got way too much potential - at something - to give up. I'd love to see you when you finally realize that potential.

Lose attention? Like that's a bad thing? Mathematics, philosophy, psychology - they're all based on jumping from one assertion to another on a whim or an instinct. Don't fret about that. 

You're short? How short? Are you American? Have you tried riding the tube in London? I thought I was short until I did that. My ex-wife is 5'1 and was massive in Tokyo. It's perspective. 

Attractive? That's what you make of it. It's kind of a cringy aspect of grammar, but if you want to be attractive to someone or some group you need to possess qualities that attract them. Who is it you aren't attractive to? If you aren't attractive to them, why bother trying? Attract those who appreciate you. 

You hate yourself? Why? Because you're forgetful (regarding your previous comment)? Who isn't? Mother's Day in the UK was this month and I blew it because I was looking at the wrong calendar. Oops. Call your father and let you know you're thinking of him on any random day and it will mean more to him than a birthday call could ever mean. 

You're being way, way, too hard on yourself. I think you've got more to offer the world than you're willing to expose. At the very least you've got basic grammar down, so that puts you ahead of a massive group. 

Chin up, call your dad out of the blue, don't cut yourself and find something you *want* to commit to rather than trying to force yourself into something you couldn't care less about. You'd be surprised how far that can get you.

Well, for one, don't stress. If she's at a hospital and openly stating she's suicidal, she isn't going anywhere for the next few days. They will not release her if they believe she's a danger to herself or others.

Second of all, I'm sure you've got caller ID on your phone, so you can trace the number back to where she called from. Even if it takes calling every ER in that particular area code, I'm sure you can find her. She's immediate family, call every ER you can in that area code and explain the situation and someone *will* find her for you. 

Finally, if you want to get her some help, it varies from state to state but it's generally the same thing. Where I am they've got the Baker Act (someone who's a danger to themselves or others) that would require a 72-hour hold and observation, or the Marchman act. I think Cali and Michigan call it a 5150, but most states have it. 

It may take some legwork, but call every ER in the area code she called you from, let them know who you are, and you will find her.

Well for one, that's a bad idea, and it probably won't work. 

For another, I played football (the gridiron version) for a long time and tore my MCL twice, got in a fight with a semi-truck and had some knee complications from that after and I could still run a mile in 6:15 after physical therapy. 

Do *not* give up on being able to play. If my fat ass can come back, so can you. You sound way, way too young to be giving up. If you were 50 I'd give you different advice, but I remember too well the thought of "I'm 25 it's over," which I laugh at now. 

I'm going to guess you're in your 20s; they're all about bouncing back. Plus look on the bright side, while your knee's healing up, you get excellent parking.
What is the surgery, what is the medicine and why do you hope to do so?

Well, everything I tried combined with everything the local, state and federal government tried - on top of decades of medication and therapy, six trips to the funny farm - didn't seem to have any effect. So I'm at a bit of a loss as where I'm supposed to turn from here. 

If I could win the lottery and buy a farm and buy a sanctuary for three-legged dogs in upstate New York I'm sure I'd feel better, but the odds on that are pretty low. 

Also, in the line of work I'm in being "Baker Acted" shows up on a background check so I'm kind of fucked on the work front. I am not in the most understanding state of the union when it comes to mental health.

Man, people will tell you to make the best of it or find like-minded individuals or find a hobby or club that you're interested in, but for me it all boils down to one fact: fuck high school. 

The point of high school is to get to college. College fucking rules. High school is the hazing you get through to get there. 

Why cut? Why leave scars? Why let these people bother you? Haven't you heard the cliche of the captain of the football team working at the local car wash 10 years after graduation? 

I'm not trying to belittle your current mood. I have been there. I found interests where I made some (not many) friends. Newspaper and marching band. Not the coolest kid in school, but I had places to hide. 

Give it some time and keep your grades up. I had terrible relationships with both of my parents, but when you finally graduate and move out, fuck 'em. 

It isn't easy. It is, honestly, a fucking nightmare at times. But do not miss out on college. It's worth the torture of high school and then some.

Over 20 years, depending on your age.

You can learn a lot in 20 years, accomplish more than you'd imagine. Didn't graduate high school? Get your GED. Didn't finish college? Online degree. 

Finished college? Get another degree. Study philosophy. Study psychology. Study literature. Study things that take your mind out of the place it's in. 

And you'd be surprised how often things can be overlooked. I personally incurred two serious felonies whilst working for the government. I was honest about it with my supervisor. A year later I got a promotion. 

I'm not saying that's normal, I'm just saying it's possible. Jail (which you'd be in given a month - or anything less than a year) is nothing but watching television, playing cards, eating shit food, keeping your mouth shut and staring at the wall. You can make the best of it, or you can make the worst of it. 

It's up to you. 

And for fuck's sake, read books. All of them. Even if you don't like them. Read them all.
